newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia stocks rally at open after Dow record.
newsitem.headline: Australia stocks rally at open after Dow record.

text.p: Australian shares opened solidly higher on Friday as the market responded predictably to the Dow's fresh record high close on Thursday as U.S. traders were encouraged by good earnings news.
At 10.20 a.m. (0020 GMT), the All Ordinaries index was 14.6 points higher at 2,368.4.
The December share price index was up 20 points at 2,393 and at a 24.6 point premium to the underlying index.
Brokers said early interest was targeted on major resource issues and the bank sector which was recovering slightly from a sell-off on Thursday.

"Rate cut hopes were diminished by the Reserve Bank's quarterly bulletin, but I think the market still believes an easing is still likely, it just may take a little longer than anticipated," a dealer at a Sydney-based brokerage said.
The dealer said all the major banks had opened slightly higher and most of the regionals were steady to higher.
Underpinning the market's early gains was a strong performance from the resources sector after base metals prices improved on the London Metal Exchange on Thursday.
"Base metal prices have been a burden on the market for ages so these signs of strength are encouraging," the dealer said.

In other trade, the shares of Woodside Petroleum opened much firmer after the company said on Thursday that partners in the North-West Shelf liquefied natural gas project had agreed to a A$6.0 billion (US$4.8 billion) expansion.
At 11.45 a.m. (0145 GMT), Woodside shares were 12 cents higher at A$8.97 .

Mayne Nickless shares were weaker early on uncertainty surrounding the proposed float of Optus Communications, in which Mayne has a 25 percent stake. At 11.45 a.m. (0145 GMT), Mayne shares were 13 cents weaker at A$8.15.

Scrap metal recycler Simsmetal also opened lower in response to the company's first quarter profit slump and its forecast of an even weaker 1996/97 second quarter. Simsmetal shares were 16 cents weaker at A$6.88 at 11.45 a.m..
